{"self_assessment": "Impact: I took the tail (stroke 3) as Leo assigned and laid the forked tail on the right, which is the fish's most telling feature. When Leo spotted that the lower fork wasn't joined to the tail junction, I took that handoff and fixed it. By our traces, the start then knocked over everything standing. I also inspected the nose and confirmed the chain carried through, with only a stray curl loose. I can't say yet whether the judge will recognize the fish. The outline looks like a fish to me, but I haven't seen it fall. We never added an eye, which would have helped.

Execution: I started the tail as the body reached the junction, and the upper half connected on the first pass. The lower fork stalled, and I was slow to notice because I was reporting it as fine before Leo caught the problem. I fixed it once it was flagged, then checked the chain. I should have inspected the lower fork myself earlier instead of trusting the look of it. From the five-minute mark I kept my hands off to avoid bumps and left no loose pieces.

Collaboration: I kept my updates short and specific, told Priya to stop adding at the nose, and backed up Maya's removal of the curl. I stayed out of other people's areas. I was quiet for stretches, and I could have offered help on the nose or belly joints when they were the bottleneck.

Leadership: Leo set direction and I followed it. I didn't take the lead on anything beyond my own stroke. I stepped up on the handoff and the verification, but I was mostly a reliable teammate rather than someone steering the table. I'd like to be quicker to flag risks and offer help when my own piece is done."}
